name: LM35
description: Precision analog temperature sensor whose output voltage is linearly proportional to temperature in degrees Celsius at 10 mV/C. Calibrated directly in Celsius, it needs no external calibration or trimming. It runs from a 4 to 30 V single supply and draws under 60 uA, giving minimal self-heating. The 0 mV = 0 C transfer characteristic is simple to read but means it cannot output negative voltages on a single supply.

pins.name: Vout
pins.description: analog output, 10 mV per degree Celsius

typical_application: Direct Celsius temperature readout into an ADC or analog meter for thermostats, power-supply thermal monitoring, and general ambient sensing.
gotchas: on a single supply the LM35 cannot read below 0 C because the output cannot go negative; sub-zero sensing needs a negative bias resistor to a -Vs rail
TO-92 pin order (flat face toward you, leads down) is +Vs, Vout, GND left-to-right
output is 0 V at 0 C (not offset like the TMP36), so 25 C = 250 mV
long wires or capacitive loads on Vout can cause oscillation; may need a series R / load cap per datasheet
self-heating is low but mounting and airflow still affect accuracy
do not confuse with the LM34 (Fahrenheit), which has an identical pinout but a different scale
